newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya approves sale of eight state firms.
newsitem.headline: Kenya approves sale of eight state firms.

text.p: Kenya said on Monday it had approved the sale of state holdings in eight firms as part of its western-backed economic reform programme.

George Mitine, investment secretary and coordinator of the government's Parastatal Reform Programme Committee (PRPC), said in a statement that the divestiture of state-owned Industrial and Commercial Development Corporation (ICDC) shareholdings in a number of firms including General Motors had been approved.
Mitine said ICDC shares would be sold to existing General Motors shareholders at a negotiable price on the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE).
Mitine said the government of President Daniel arap Moi had also approved Mount Kenya Bottler's divestiture, where ICDC holds some 20.9 percent shares.
He said ICDC would simultaneously carry out similar moves in Kisii Bottlers and Rift Valley Bottlers.

Mitine said the PRPC had also sanctioned the winding up of Rehabilitation Advisory Services (RAS), where the public shareholding was held by ICDC, Development Finance Company of Kenya and the Industrial Development Bank.

"RAS was previously categorised under strategic parastatals which were not to be sold, but in light of changed business environment brought about by the liberalisation of the economy, its operations were found to be no longer effective," Mitine said.
Mitine said the PRPC had also ratified a decision by government to dilute its shareholding in commercial bank Stanbic Kenya.
Kenyan government officials say some 136 state companies have been sold in three years.
Independent economists and opposition leaders have persistently argued for the outright sale of state-owned firms.
